newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP weakens zloty to help exports -analysts.
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP weakens zloty to help exports -analysts.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland (NBP) has intervened for the second day on Friday to weaken the zloty to help export growth while maintaining high interest rates to keep a lid on demand and imports, analysts said on Friday.

In a series of currency-buying interventions on Thursday and Friday the central bank bought some $290 million and pounded the bullish zloty down to 2.5 percent from the trading band centre from above 3.2 percent.

It also kept its 273-day paper's average yield flat at 22.00 percent and its benchmark 14-day reverse repo rate at 22.15 percent on Friday despite a drop in inflation to 16.6 percent in March year-on-year from 17.3 percent in February.

The NBP, the finance ministry and independent economists agree Poland has every chance to bring inflation down to the targeted 13-percent year-on-year in December. They also agree that the central bank is preoccupied with the trade balance and hence its reluctance to let zloty rise.
"The NBP is looking at Poland's trade balance, which is deteriorating, and is intervening to weaken the zloty to stimulate exports growth," said Andrzej Ladko, chief dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
"It also keeps high real interest rates to keep domestic demand down and thus cap imports growth," he said.

The bank has frequently expressed concern over the widening current account gap and said it would keep real interest rates rising to cool down domestic demand seen in the fast growth of credit for the economy.
Poland's current account deficit in February rose to $1.13 billion from $899 million in January against $1.35 billion in the whole of 1996.

The trade gap jumped to $2.18 billion in the first two months of this year from $706 million in January and $8.15 in the whole of 1996 as imports keep rising at about 30 percent in year-on-year terms while exports at about nine percent.

Analysts said that to offset the monetary effect of the interventions, the central bank offered on Friday a huge 1.2 billion zloty reverse repo and a 300 million zloty sale of its 273-day bills -- the longest the bank has been selling.

"It is a safe moment because inflation is falling, but nevertheless the NBP sterilised the purchases with open market operations on Friday," said Zbigniew Chmielewski chief dealer at ING Bank in Wrasaw.
Analysts said for the weaker zloty to have an effect on Poland's foreign trade, the central bank is likely to keep the zloty anchored around the 2.5 percent from parity level for some time.
"If they did it to stimulate exports, they will have to keep that level for a while," said Marek Zelinski, analyst at Bank Slaski SA.
